patch.objective: Manage boundaries, dual relationships, conflicts of interest and self-disclosure, including power differences and online contact

sources.cite: ASWB Examination Guidebook (August 2026), Clinical content outline: I Values and Ethics, 36% (IB 'Professional boundaries in the social worker-client/client system relationship (e.g., power differences, influence, privilege, conflicts of interest, self-disclosure, dual relationships)'); the 2026 blueprint in use from 2026-08-03
sources.note: Read in full 2026-11-14 for the course outline (REQ-286).

sources.cite: NASW Code of Ethics (approved 1996, revised 2021): 1.06(c) dual relationships and clear boundaries when unavoidable; 1.06(h) clients' requests on social networking sites; 1.13(b) bartering
sources.note: Standards 1-3 read in full 2026-11-14 for the course (REQ-286); as the course records them (not quotations): 1.06(c) no dual or multiple relationships where there is a risk of exploitation or potential harm, and when they are unavoidable, clear, culturally sensitive boundaries; 1.06(h) avoid accepting clients' requests on social networking sites; 1.13(b) bartering only in very limited circumstances (accepted locally, essential to services, negotiated without coercion, at the client's initiative, with informed consent). NASW's Delegate Assembly votes on proposed amendments on 2026-11-18; recheck by 2026-12-15.
